# Cross-column references for lossless table deltas

The input, wire budget and 5% development threshold follow the [original design](../development.md). After the first failure, we examined changed Tate fields. A title and the corresponding object URL often change together, and measurements can move across columns. These observations motivate a development hypothesis that aligned values from the same row describe some edits more cheaply than a patch against the same cell alone. Both Tate intervals informed this design.

Encode inserted rows and removed keys in full. For surviving records, transmit the changed row positions in each column as deltas, and a separate stream of edits in the same order. The own-cell control chooses between a new string and a sequence of literals and substring copies from the old cell. The candidate additionally considers any other old value in the row, a previously decoded new value and substitution of an earlier changed field into the old current cell. The substituted field can be literal or URL-normalized (Unicode decomposition, ASCII transliteration by dropping non-ASCII characters, lowercase and hyphenated nonalphanumeric runs). The candidate pays for every source reference and residual edit. Choose the shortest uncompressed UTF-8 JSON instruction, resolving ties in enumeration order. Compress the complete JSON patch using XZ preset 6. Both arms share the same edit aligner, sparse row masks, compression and field order.

Compare both arms against the first study's six round-tripped controls and against bsdiff 4.3. Reassemble each canonical target and require equality. Score the candidate on both development intervals, with the 5% margin relative to each comparator, including its matched own-cell ablation. Only after the development screen succeeds should a fixed-model experiment select untouched independent catalogue releases prospectively and assess uncertainty at publisher level.
